model.ml_customer_segmentation.int_custo.name: int_customer_balance_metrics
model.ml_customer_segmentation.int_custo.raw_code:
{{ config(
    alias='int_customer_balance_metrics',
    materialized='table'
) }}

with source as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_customer_monthly_balance') }}

)

select
    customer_id,

    -- Average balance across all available months
    avg(average_balance_in_month) as avg_monthly_balance,

    -- Volatility = stddev / avg balance, capped at 3.0
    -- If denominator is too small, force capped high-volatility value
    case
        when abs(avg(average_balance_in_month)) < 1000 then 3.0
        else least(
            3.0,
            coalesce(
                stddev_samp(average_balance_in_month)
                / nullif(abs(avg(average_balance_in_month)), 0),
                0
            )
        )
    end as balance_volatility_ratio,

    -- Growth compares recent 3 months vs earliest 3 months, then clamps to [-1, 3]
    greatest(
        -1.0,
        least(
            3.0,
            (
                avg(case when balance_month_rank_desc <= 3 then closing_balance end)
                - avg(case when balance_month_rank_asc <= 3 then closing_balance end)
            )
            /
            (
                abs(avg(case when balance_month_rank_asc <= 3 then closing_balance end)) + 1
            )
        )
    ) as balance_growth_rate,

    -- Number of months where account went into overdraft
    sum(case when overdraft_flag = 'Y' then 1 else 0 end) as overdraft_month_count

from source
group by customer_id

model.ml_customer_segmentation.int_custo.raw_code:
{{ config(
    alias='int_customer_txn_metrics',
    materialized='table'
) }}

with params as (

    -- Fixed reference date for recency metrics
    select to_date('{{ var("reference_date", "2026-08-01") }}') as reference_date

),

txns as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_customer_txn_base') }}

),

profile as (

    -- Brings in effective_months for frequency denominators
    select *
    from {{ ref('int_customer_profile') }}

)

select
    t.customer_id,

    -- Average completed transactions per effective month
    count(*) / nullif(p.effective_months, 0)::float as txn_frequency_per_month,

    -- Share of months with at least one completed transaction
    count(distinct t.txn_month) / nullif(p.effective_months, 0)::float as active_months_ratio,

    -- Recency from latest transaction date to reference date
    datediff('day', max(t.transaction_date), prm.reference_date) as days_since_last_txn,

    -- Average transaction size in INR
    avg(abs(t.amount_inr)) as avg_txn_amount,

    -- Coefficient of variation - stddev / mean
    coalesce(
        stddev_samp(abs(t.amount_inr)) / nullif(avg(abs(t.amount_inr)), 0),
        0
    ) as txn_amount_cv,

    -- Share of high-value transactions
    avg(t.is_high_value) as high_value_txn_ratio,

    -- Net balance between credits and debits

### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
